title: Candidate comms are never actually delivered by default — the outbox is a terminal, recruiter-only sink; no email/SMS provider exists
expected: The acknowledgement (with the status link), the rejection, and every later stage comm reach the candidate on a real channel — a candidate can't read a simulated email.
got: sendComm routes to OutboxChannel by default: status 'queued' is documented as a *terminal* dev state — 'the outbox IS the delivery target'. Real delivery exists only when COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL is set, and even then it is a generic HTTP webhook relay POSTing a kp.comm.v1 envelope — not a first-party email/SMS provider (no SendGrid/SES/Twilio/nodemailer dependency anywhere in package.json or app/_lib). The only candidate-readable rendering of these messages is the recruiter-side Outbox (CommsCenter.tsx). Mitigation that keeps the journey alive: the conversational apply renders the status link in-page on success, so a candidate who saves it can pull their status without any email.
evidence: app/_lib/comms.ts:36-42 (OutboxChannel — 'queued' is terminal, the row is both the delivered artifact and the audit entry)
app/_lib/comms.ts:97-100 (getCommsChannel — WebhookChannel only when COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL is set)
app/_lib/comms.ts:53-64 (WebhookChannel — generic relay, 'wire to SendGrid / a mail relay / Zapier / an ATS')
app/features/sub_channels/CommsCenter.tsx:6-17 (the outbox viewer lives in the authed recruiter workspace)
app/apply/[id]/ConversationalApply.tsx:443-450 (in-page 'Track your application status' link — the pull-based mitigation)
scope_note: The pluggable-channel design is deliberate and documented (app/_lib/comms.ts:6-9, docs/COMMS_DELIVERY.md); dead-letters are alerted loudly. Severity stays major (not dropped for demo scope) because candidate-facing copy actively asserts delivery — see capst-l1-002.
l2_priority: Apply live as a candidate and confirm what actually arrives: with no COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL, verify the ack exists only in the recruiter Outbox; if a relay URL is configured, verify a real message leaves the box and carries the status + erasure links.
suggested_acceptance: Either a real provider adapter (SMTP/SendGrid) behind the same CommsChannel seam, or candidate-facing copy that stops promising email until one is configured.

title: Quick-apply leads get NO status link at all — and are told 'We've emailed you a confirmation'
expected: Both apply paths end with status visibility. The journey's DoD: a status link shows where the candidate stands without contacting the recruiter.
got: Only the conversational path mints and returns a statusToken. The quick-apply POST response carries leadToken but no statusToken (the success screen renders no status link), and the quick lead's acknowledgement goes through intakeLead → dispatchApplicationReceived with only { enrichLink } — the statusLine is appended solely when opts.statusLink is passed, which lead-intake never does. So Tereza's fastest path (the one built for her phone) ends in exactly the black hole she fears until she completes the 2-minute enrichment chat. Worse, the quick success copy says 'We've emailed you a confirmation' (quick.acceptedMessage, en+cs) — with the default outbox channel (capst-l1-001) that email was never delivered, so the one claim the surface makes about follow-up is false by default.
evidence: app/api/apply/[id]/quick/route.ts:132-140 (accept responses return leadToken only — no statusToken)
app/apply/[id]/quick/QuickApplyForm.tsx:101-128 (done screen: enrichment CTA only, no status link)
app/_lib/lead-intake.ts:129-138,210 (ack passes { enrichLink } only)
app/_lib/comms-dispatch.ts:140-146 (statusLine appended only when opts.statusLink is given)
app/api/apply/[id]/route.ts:474-495 (contrast: conversational path mints the token once, puts it in BOTH the ack email and the JSON response)
messages/en.json + messages/cs.json apply.quick.acceptedMessage ('We've emailed you a confirmation' / 'Potvrzení jsme vám poslali e-mailem')
l2_priority: Submit a quick apply live; confirm the success screen and the outbox ack carry no /status/ link, and that the copy still claims an email was sent.
suggested_acceptance: Quick route mints getOrCreateStatusLink(entry.id) like the conversational route, returns it in the JSON, renders it on the success screen, and passes statusLink into the ack.

title: On quick apply the data-processing consent statement appears only AFTER submitting — but submitting IS the consent
expected: Journey DoD: 'AI-use + GDPR data-processing disclosure is visible at the point of consent; submitting IS the consent, with a stated retention window and an erasure path.' The retention/consent sentence must be readable BEFORE the candidate taps Apply.
got: The quick form renders <AiDisclosure /> WITHOUT showDataConsent pre-submit (title + 'AI assists, a human decides' + regime line show; the 'By submitting, you agree we may process your personal data … up to 12 months … erasure' sentence does not). The showDataConsent variant is mounted only on the post-submit done screen — after recordEntryConsent has already stamped consent + a 12-month expiry at intake. The conversational path gets this right: <AiDisclosure showDataConsent /> is pinned under the chat for the whole flow. Not a pre-ticked trap (nothing is ticked at all), but consent-by-submission with the statement shown after the fact fails the point-of-consent bar.
evidence: app/apply/[id]/quick/QuickApplyForm.tsx:228 (pre-submit: <AiDisclosure className="mt-6" /> — no showDataConsent)
app/apply/[id]/quick/QuickApplyForm.tsx:126 (post-submit done screen: <AiDisclosure … showDataConsent />)
app/_lib/lead-intake.ts:149,198,209 (recordLeadConsent → recordEntryConsent fires at submit)
app/_components/AiDisclosure.tsx:60 (dataConsent line renders only when showDataConsent)
app/apply/[id]/ConversationalApply.tsx:601 (conversational path shows the full disclosure throughout — the correct pattern)
l2_priority: Confirm live that the quick form's pre-submit view really omits the retention sentence in both locales, and that it appears on the done screen.
suggested_acceptance: One-line fix: pass showDataConsent on the form-state AiDisclosure at QuickApplyForm.tsx:228.

title: The disclosure's 'nothing adverse is decided automatically' overstates what the machinery does
expected: The AI-use disclosure is accurate — an engineer (and a regulator) reading it should find the code matches the claim.
got: aiDisclosure.body promises 'A human reviews and makes every advance, offer, and rejection decision; nothing adverse is decided automatically.' Two automated adverse paths exist: (1) the KO gate auto-declines an applicant with no human in the loop — deterministic, rule-based on the candidate's own answers, and audited, but still an automatic adverse outcome; (2) the screening wave auto-rejects the bottom cohort by AI match score with actor 'system' and dispatches automated rejections — a human approves the reviewed SET (approval token + Art.22-style sealed record + fairness fail-closed gate), which is batch-level oversight, not the per-decision human review the sentence claims.
evidence: messages/en.json aiDisclosure.body (and the cs equivalent)
app/api/apply/[id]/route.ts:238-253 (KO fail → automatic decline, no human review; audited via recordKnockoutDecline)
app/_lib/screen-wave.ts:12-17 (module contract: 'the screening first wave of automated decisions … auto-reject the bottom …')
app/_lib/screen-wave.ts:253,281 (actOnPipelineEntry(…, actor: 'system') + dispatchRejection(updated, { automated: true }))
app/_lib/screen-wave.ts:266-272 (mitigation: sealed Art.22 record with approvedBy — batch-level human approval)
scope_note: Mitigations are real: KO gates are eligibility rules the candidate answers knowingly, the wave requires operator approval and fails closed for fairness-protected archetypes, and every auto-decision is audited. The gap is the absoluteness of the candidate-facing sentence, not a hidden black box.
suggested_acceptance: Soften/precision-fit the disclosure copy (e.g. 'eligibility questions are checked automatically; a human reviews every AI-assisted screening decision before it is applied') so it matches the batch-approval reality.

title: The consent copy hardcodes '12 months' while the actual retention TTL is env-configurable
expected: The retention window the candidate consents to matches what the system enforces.
got: aiDisclosure.dataConsent states 'up to 12 months' verbatim in both catalogs, but the enforced TTL is KP_CONSENT_TTL_DAYS (1..3650 days, default 365) — a deployment that legitimately tunes retention per its legal basis (the code comment explicitly invites this) would silently make the disclosed number wrong at the exact point of consent.
evidence: app/_lib/consent.ts:14-18 (defaultConsentTtlDays — env-configurable, 'a deployment SHOULD set it for its legal basis')
messages/en.json aiDisclosure.dataConsent ('up to 12 months'); messages/cs.json ('po dobu až 12 měsíců')
app/api/apply/[id]/route.ts:447-452 (consent recorded with that TTL at submit)
suggested_acceptance: Interpolate the live TTL (e.g. surface CONSENT_TTL_DAYS through /api/compliance, which AiDisclosure already fetches) into the dataConsent string.

title: The status page has no language switcher and the emailed status link isn't locale-pinned
expected: APP4 gave the apply pages their own LanguageSwitcher precisely because candidates can't reach the workspace switcher; the status page — opened weeks later, possibly on another device — deserves the same.
got: /status/[token] renders no LanguageSwitcher (the apply and quick pages both mount one), and the ack email's status link is built bare while the enrichment link IS pinned with ?lang={applicantLocale}. Mitigated in the common case by cookie → Accept-Language → default resolution (a Czech phone gets Czech), so this bites only when the browser locale differs from the application language — then Tereza reads her status in English with no way to switch on-page.
evidence: app/status/[token]/page.tsx:61-128 (no LanguageSwitcher anywhere on the page)
app/apply/[id]/page.tsx:84-86 + app/apply/[id]/quick/page.tsx:58-60 (the switcher the apply surfaces got)
app/api/apply/[id]/route.ts:479 (status link built without ?lang=)
app/api/apply/[id]/quick/route.ts:106 (contrast: enrichLink pinned with ?lang=${applicantLocale})
i18n/server.ts:9-15 (cookie → Accept-Language → 'en' default — the mitigation)
l2_priority: Open a minted /status/ link in a browser with an en locale after applying in cs — confirm the mismatch and the absence of an on-page switch.
suggested_acceptance: Mount LanguageSwitcher on the status page and pin ?lang= on the emailed status link (the entry already stores locale).

got: The status projection is a small friendly enum with terminal states rendered honestly (a company-side close reads 'not selected', a role filled reads not_selected 'without implying a merit rejection'); the public API returns only status/jobTitle/company/updatedAt — never internal ids, names, scores, or reasoning; the token is unguessable and deliberately NOT the entry PK (an IDOR handle elsewhere); a re-apply reuses the ORIGINAL entry so the candidate keeps ONE stable status link; the conversational flow mints the token once so email and in-page link can never diverge. title: STRENGTH — the apply flow is genuinely quick, resilient, and role-grounded (no bait-and-switch)
got: The chat script is server-built from the REAL job — greeting names the role+company, KO questions derive from job.location/workMode/languages (never boilerplate; ko_mode/ko_lang only appear when the job warrants them) — and paints on hydration with zero round-trip. ~8-10 short steps for an experienced applicant, every optional step skippable (CV, GitHub), CV upload pre-fills name/email as editable defaults, drafts survive a refresh/lost signal with a start-fresh escape, a failed final submit distinguishes retryable (re-POST saved answers) from rejected input (start over) so a blip never eats the conversation, email/GitHub typos are caught inline at their own step, and the chat is a screen-reader-live log with per-step focus management. The quick path is honestly ≤30s (2 fields + the same KO contract, honeypot-defended). Both locales are complete and the Czech is native-quality, not machine-translated.

title: STRENGTH — candidate comms are deterministic, humane, locale-pinned, and carry GDPR self-service
